result.title: Curriculum-Guided Acquisition of Hierarchical Task Knowledge from LLM-Generated Experience
result.comment: 15 pages, 2 figures, 1 table. Presented at the Thirteenth Annual Conference on Advances in Cognitive Systems (ACS 2026)
result.summary: Hierarchical task knowledge enables efficient problem solving by allowing previously acquired skills to be reused across tasks and problem instances. In this paper, we investigate curriculum-guided acquisition of hierarchical task knowledge in an HTN learning framework. We compare three approaches: online learning during problem solving, human-designed curricula, and an automated curriculum generation procedure that derives learning experiences from verified LLM-generated solution traces. The proposed procedure solves small training problems with an LLM, extracts task accomplishment information, and transforms it into ordered sequences of state-task learning problems for HTN method acquisition. We evaluate the three approaches across multiple planning domains. The results demonstrate that automatically generated curricula recover much of the benefit of expert-designed curricula while substantially reducing the token cost of online hierarchical knowledge acquisition.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 HTN 学习框架中比较三种层级任务知识获取方式——解题过程中的在线学习、人工设计课程、以及从经核验的 LLM 生成解题轨迹自动导出课程（将其转为有序的 state-task 学习问题序列），并在多个规划域上评估效果与 token 成本。
